title: Throughput-Optimal Scheduling Algorithms for LLM Inference and AI Agents
technique: queueing-theoretic proof that work-conserving (K-FCFS) batch schedulers achieve maximal stable throughput; classifies Orca/Sarathi-Serve as throughput-optimal, FasterTransformer/vanilla vLLM as not

optimized_metrics.evidence: We prove that a large class of 'work-conserving' scheduling algorithms achieve maximum throughput for both individual requests and AI-agent workloads
What is the maximal throughput of an LLM inference system, and which batch scheduling algorithms can achieve it?

headline_claim.text: Orca and Sarathi-Serve are throughput-optimal, reassuring practitioners, while FasterTransformer and vanilla vLLM are not maximally stable and should be used with caution.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Throughput measures the token generation rate within a given timeframe.
metric_definitions.notes: informal; the formal notion is queueing-stability throughput: 'A scheduling algorithm is said to achieve throughput λ if the associated DTMC {X(n), n ∈ N} is irreducible and positive recurrent when the arrival rate is λ' (§3.2) - i.e. max sustainable request arrival rate (THR_REQ)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Inference latency represents the time required to complete a request from start to finish; common latency metrics include TTFT (time to first token, measuring prefill latency) and TBT (time between tokens, measuring decoding latency).
SLO attainment measures the percentage (e.g., 99%) of requests fulfilled within a predefined latency target.
a scheduling algorithm π is said to be work-conserving if π(x) forms a batch of token load b = bmax whenever possible.

load_regime: request-rate sweep / fixed Poisson arrival rate (14 QPS, Fig 1) and trace replay (1.2 QPS coding trace); stability analysis
tradeoff_acknowledged: Table 3: Sarathi-Serve best E2E and prefill latency but FasterTransformer has lowest TBT - 'a trade-off between prefill responsiveness and decode smoothness'; small token budget (128) adds chunked-prefill overhead
workloads: Poisson synthetic (129 prefill / 112 decode tokens), production conversation and coding traces (Splitwise), ShareGPT for batch-time fits
extractor_notes: Primarily theory. Paper says 'This paper focuses on throughput and leaves the study of SLO attainment to future work.' Throughput = stability region (max arrival rate), not measured tokens/s; coded THR_REQ. Latency (E2E/TTFT/TBT) only a preliminary appendix-style study (Table 3).

tail_audit.metrics: E2E/TTFT/TBT median/P90/P95/P99 in appendix experiment table only; tail-latency objectives listed as future work
